scenario.title: SVC returns the wrong value - result written to the live r0, not the stacked r0
scenario.description: The kernel from P06 with one bug in the SVC handler: after handling write(), it puts the return value 1 into the register r0 instead of into the stacked r0 of the caller's exception frame. On exception return the hardware pops the frame and overwrites r0 with the stacked value, which is still the argument (the character code). Task B checks the return value of every write() and counts the failures. The character is still printed, so the system looks healthy from the outside.

expected.summary: No faults, the alphabet is printed, but every write() returns its argument instead of 1, so svc_errors climbs and task B reports it.

scenario.what_to_look_for: Each kernel syscall event for write says "return value 1 written to the LIVE r0 (lost ...)". The following exception_return pops the frame: its popped_frame.r0 is the character (0x41, 0x42 ...), and in the viewer's register panel r0 after the return is that character, not 1. Task B's marker "write() returned a wrong value" follows every call and the global svc_errors grows. Compare with P06, where svc_errors stays 0 and the syscall event says "written to the stacked r0 at 0x2000....".
likely_root_causes: The SVC handler (C function) returns its result normally, and the assembly wrapper never stores r0 into the frame.
The handler writes the frame through the wrong stack pointer (MSP instead of PSP), so it updates some other memory and the caller's frame keeps the argument.
The frame pointer passed to the C dispatcher is computed before the hardware frame (off by 32 bytes), so 'frame[0] = result' lands in the wrong word.
how_to_debug: Break at the end of the SVC handler: 'x/8xw $psp' and check word 0 (stacked r0) holds the result before 'bx lr'.
Step over the exception return ('stepi' on bx lr) and 'p/x $r0' in the task: it equals the stacked word, whatever the handler left in the live r0.
Write a test system call that returns a constant (e.g. 0x1234) and check it from a task.
scenario.what_this_means: An exception return restores r0-r3, r12, lr, pc and xPSR from the stack, so for the caller of svc the stacked frame IS the register file. Arguments are read from it and results must be written into it. Anything written to the live registers is overwritten by the hardware on the way out.
scenario.hidden_symptom: Output appears normally, but every system call reports failure to its caller.
